<reflection>
The first experiment provided a baseline with moderate substrate and catalyst concentrations. The fitting results show that many mechanisms have very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, with M7 (substrate inhibition) slightly better but not decisively so. M4 and M5 are clear outliers with high NLL, so they can be ruled out. The remaining 18 mechanisms are still plausible, as their NLLs differ by less than 1.1 units. The aim of the first experiment was to obtain initial discrimination; it succeeded in eliminating two mechanisms but left a highly degenerate set. Therefore, a new experiment is needed to break this degeneracy by probing conditions where the mechanisms predict different behaviors.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Lowering the catalyst concentration to 0.001 M (10-fold lower than the first experiment) will make the reaction slower and more sensitive to mechanistic details. Activation mechanisms (M6, M8) may exhibit a lag phase if activation is slow relative to turnover. Dimerization mechanisms (M2, M3) will show a nonlinear dependence of rate on catalyst concentration. Deactivation mechanisms (M9-M20) may become more pronounced if deactivation is concentration-dependent. Reducing substrate to 1.0 M avoids saturation and may help distinguish substrate inhibition (M7) from others. This condition explores a different region of concentration space, providing complementary information to the first run. The progress curve shape and initial rate should differ across mechanisms, enhancing discrimination across the entire set rather than just the top few.
</hypothesis>
